To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the MREs in the coding and non-coded RNAs are the crosstalk hub of gene regulation and ceRNAs are the new entrants in this crosstalk.
miRNAs and ceRNAs play an important role in the regulation of genes involved in the pathogenesis of various diseases.
ceRNAs are the emerging players that are involved in miRNA-mediated gene regulation.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the identification, characterization and function of ceRNAs.
understanding the complexities in miRNA mediated gene regulatory networks and the emerging role of ceRNAs in this context.
deciphering the role of ceRNAs and their MREs in regulating gene expression and their impact on human diseases.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the ceRNA hypothesis provides a new dimension to the intricate network of gene regulation.
miRNAs are the key regulators that control gene expression, and ceRNAs are the new players that modulate the expression of miRNAs.
ceRNA-mediated crosstalk is a complex phenomenon, which has to be deciphered by a combination of computational and experimental approaches.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the ceRNA paradigm is a new dimension to the miRNA world and is an exciting new field of research.
the miRNAs and ceRNAs are the two sides of the same coin and the miRNA-MREs- ceRNA network is the coin itself.
the ceRNA hypothesis is a powerful tool to understand gene regulation, which is a complex network of interactions.
The main takeaway from our work is that
ceRNAs are not merely passive recipients of miRNA-mediated regulation but are also active regulators that can influence each other.
the MREs are the hubs for gene crosstalk and ceRNAs are the mediators of this crosstalk.
miRNAs can act in a non-linear fashion, and the miRNA-mediated ceRNA crosstalk is a key determinant in gene expression.
